subject: Velox: log integrity assurance and confirmation of no data exfiltration
messages:
From: Samir Mehta <samir@velox-fin.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: request for log verification after snapshot anomaly

Neha —

We observed an anomalous snapshot referenced in our monitoring at ~02:45 UTC on Dec 2 that shows an unexpected increase in outbound connections from the Redwood inference pool serving Velox. I wanted to escalate and ask for a quick verification that there was no data exfiltration or customer data leakage related to this spike.

Can your team confirm: 1) whether any tokens or customer payloads were written to external destinations, 2) whether any internal storage blobs or S3 objects were accessed anomalously, and 3) provide the relevant access/log artifacts we can attach to our internal incident review?

We are happy to join a call if that helps. This is high priority for our security and compliance teams.

Thanks,
Samir Mehta
Head of Infrastructure Security
Velox Financial
security@velox-fin.com

---
Attachment: snapshot-metrics-20261202.png (image/png)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: Samir Mehta <samir@velox-fin.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: request for log verification after snapshot anomaly

Hi Samir —

Thanks for flagging and sorry for the alarm. I’ve looped in Monica (Customer Reliability) and Markus (Head of Security) to run a targeted integrity sweep. Initial notes: our edge telemetry shows the same outbound spike you saw, but we have not completed payload-level correlation yet. Monica will run a KV-cache and prefix-scan; Markus will review ingress/egress connection logs, container-level network flows, and any S3 access.

We expect initial findings within ~6 business hours and will share artifacts (redacted traces, log slices, and a short summary). If you’d like a call, Monica can do a 30-min slot today at 1pm PT — otherwise we’ll follow up over email.

Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment: request_acknowledgement.txt (text)

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Samir Mehta <samir@velox-fin.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: request for log verification after snapshot anomaly

Samir / Neha / Monica —

Triage summary (executive): we completed a forensic scan across the serving pool and long-term telemetry for the timeframe 2026-12-02T02:30:00Z - 2026-12-02T03:15:00Z. Key findings: 

- No evidence of outbound transfers of persisted customer payloads. We scanned network flows for large payload outbound transfers and cross-checked with S3 Put object events; none matched in the time window.
- KV cache inspection: no externalized cache dumps or write operations to customer-owned buckets. We validated cache eviction and prefix logs against expected policies.
- Control-plane access: only internal operator accounts (service identities) made requests; there are no unusual IAM role escalations.
- TLS intercepts / middleboxes: none detected in our egress path; connections were to known provider IPs.

Artifacts attached: velox_log_scan_summary.pdf (contains redacted flow timelines) and redwood_kv_cache_audit.csv (cache keys + checksums). We also uploaded a full packet-indexed slice to our secure S3: s3://redwood-telemetry/velox/2026-12-02/logs/ (read-only link available on request).

Technical notes (for your SOC): we ran the following checks: 1) per-host tcpdump-derived connection size histogram, 2) application-layer token-window correlation to detect token leakage patterns, 3) S3 server access log cross-correlation, 4) anomaly scoring vs baseline for outbound bytes per-second. All checks returned below-risk thresholds and no indicators of data exfiltration.

Next steps recommended:
- If Velox wants, we can provide an ISO-formatted CSV of the matched log slices for your ingestion into your SIEM.
- We will also include this event in our weekly audit bundle and tag as closed unless you request further escalation.

-MK
Markus Klein
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: velox_log_scan_summary.pdf; redwood_kv_cache_audit.csv

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: Samir Mehta <samir@velox-fin.com>, security@velox-fin.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Velox: log integrity assurance and confirmation of no data exfiltration

Samir —

Following up with the finalized artifacts and confirmation from our security team. As Markus summarized, our forensic and log-integrity scans show no indications of data exfiltration or unauthorized access tied to the Dec 2 snapshot anomaly. We attached the summary and the cache-audit CSV here for your records.

For your incident review, condensed conclusions we recommend recording:
- Event window: 2026-12-02T02:30:00Z - 2026-12-02T03:15:00Z
- Findings: no persisted customer payloads observed in outbound transfers; no anomalous S3 Put events; no escalation of operator/service IAM roles.
- Evidence: velox_log_scan_summary.pdf; redwood_kv_cache_audit.csv; secure S3 slice available (contact us for temporary read credentials).

If Velox requires a signed attestation or a deeper packet-level export for regulatory audit, let us know the scope and we’ll coordinate with legal and security to produce one. Otherwise we’ll mark the incident as closed on our side and include it in the Dec audit bundle.

Would you like a short closure note we can co-sign and add to the Velox incident ticket? Happy to help.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: velox_log_scan_summary.pdf (report); redwood_kv_cache_audit.csv (csv)
